w: Samarpan Din On Swamishri's last full day in Houston, the Southwest Region held Samarpan Din, where they recognised the sacrifices of countless devotees in organising and executing the Mandir Mahotsav. After Swamishri's morning puja, a special mahapuja was held for all devotees to bring peace into their lives and to fulfil their inner wishes. During the evening assembly, Swamishri explained that the most important thing to do after the construction of the Mandir is to take full advantage of it, and increase our understanding of our soul. "Once one has knowledge of the soul," he said, "one will not desire to indulge in the pleasures of the world."
Divine Moods of Swamishri

With the heavy monsoon rains many villages in Kheda district were flooded and left people marooned. On Swamishri’s instruction BAPS sadhus and volunteers provided rescue and relief. Food packets and relief materials prepared in Bochasan and Atladra mandirs were supplied by volunteers to the flood-affected victims.

At 4.00 pm Swamishri arrived for an assembly on the occasion of the solar eclipse. The assembly commenced with the Swaminarayan dhun followed by a discourse by Viveksagar Swami, bhajans by sadhus and a question-answer session with senior sadhus. The assembly concluded at 6.05 pm.

One devotee is a very big industrialist. Although he was a satsangi, years ago he used to do all his work only after consulting a tantrik, and because of this the tantrik had become a multimillionaire. When Pramukh Swami Maharaj came to know of this, Swamishri once called him and made him very firm in his refuge and conviction. Because of this he gave up all the tantrik rituals. Today he said to Swamishri, "After giving up the tantrik rituals, my business has doubled."
Running his hand along the man's neck, Swamishri said, "This kanthi (sacred necklace) is the greatest of ornaments, greater even than gold... gold... gold... gold ornaments."

Mahant Swami Maharaj came to his room and sat to have his meal. Today, the devotees who were coming on a different flight from Swamishri had arrived later than scheduled. Swamishri asked with curiosity, "Why were they late?"

One sadhu told the whole story: "Swami! Today you protected us. As we were boarding the plane, they stopped us and said, 'Get off now.' We got off. It took quite a while. We found out that one engine was faulty."
Swamishri exclaimed, "The whole plane was going to go into the sea..." Then he asked, "Which sadhus were there?"
The sadhus said, "There were eight sadhus and other sadhaks and devotees, 25 in all, including Yagnavallabhdas Swami, Gnanpriyadas Swami..."
Swamishri said, "They too would have gone."
This was the second time Swamishri said a sentence with this meaning.
The sadhus said, "You protected us."
The sadhus joked and asked, "So did Gunvatsal Swami go to Akshardham and come back?"
Swamishri said "Yes."
The sadhus said, "There was also turbulence (instability in the air caused by changes in air pressure), and we felt frightened, because we could see the sea right below."
Swamishri again said, "You were going to go into the sea."
Thanking him, the sadhus began to say to Swamishri, "It is you who protected us."
With the humility of a servant, Swamishri said, "Maharaj and Swami protected you."
Swamishri never loses, even for a moment, the awareness that Maharaj and Swami are the doers.
